items.title: Loren Schoenberg interviewed by Monk Rowe, New York City, New York, January 14, 2019

ctx.x: That there’s something to know that I don’t know. There’s nothing to know about jazz. There’s nothing to know about eating a piece of salmon. There’s nothing to know about, you know, walking down the street. There’s nothing to know about it. You like it or you don’t like it. And if you can let go of the preconceptions, if you like it and if you’re curious, maybe you’ll want to know more about it. But there’s nothing to know. I mean Jesus, there’s nothing to know about, I mean think of some of the most basic…

I love that. Because I’ve had people say, “I don’t like jazz, I don’t understand it. I like Beethoven.” And I feel like saying, “Do you understand Beethoven? What do you understand about Beethoven that makes you like it?”
